clue.text: Supporting pipes, very hot features turned off

indicators.note: a thing that features something has it within it, so one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: scalding means extremely hot

indicators.note: something turned is facing the other way, so the word it follows is read from its end

parts.note: taken as written, then read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the very hot elements in a heating system's pipes have been switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporting pipes' reads like plumbing that carries hot water, but it means the tubular framework round a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaffolding is the framework of metal tubes erected to hold workers up beside a building.

clue.text: Team player after little time runs SUV

indicators.note: after places the player's word behind the short pieces that come before it

parts.note: Chelsea is a London football club
T is the abbreviation for time
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
an actor plays parts on stage

explanation.surface: A footballer drives a sports utility vehicle, arriving after only a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea tractor is British slang for a big 4x4 driven around wealthy parts of London such as Chelsea rather than off road.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase mocks large sport utility vehicles used for school runs in affluent city districts.

clue.text: Republican leader supporting Democrat

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A Republican figurehead backs a Democrat, crossing the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' looks like a placing instruction, but here it supplies the letters FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford was a Republican who served as American president in the mid-1970s.

clue.text: First test in which I drink

indicators.note: in which says the following pieces are placed inside the word just given

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
taken as written
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Describes the first exam during which the candidate had a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Something original came earliest, before any copies or later versions were made.

clue.text: Rod we manipulated circling top of soil, one searching for water

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the shuffled letters surround the selected one
manipulated letters have been handled and moved about into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its opening letter

parts.note: the initial letter of soil

explanation.surface: Water diviners twist a rod over the ground while hunting for a hidden spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged DOWER goes round S to make DOWSER; the rod in the surface really is a dowser's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowser walks over land holding a forked stick or rod to locate underground water sources.

clue.text: Nothing has hooked a tack

indicators.note: having hooked something means holding it caught inside

parts.note: nil means zero
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler laments catching nothing but a tack on the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A tack is a small short pin with a flat head, a kind of fastening hammered into wood.

clue.text: Where hands go incessantly?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the route a watch's pointers travel over its face
second meaning: continuously, all day and night

explanation.walkthrough: Hands suggests people's hands, but they are a clock's pointers circling the dial.
explanation.definitionFit: Working nonstop through all twenty-four hours is a common idiom for doing something without a break.

clue.text: Sharp pegs or otherwise for small jumper

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the preceding letters take a different arrangement

parts.note: these two words plus the or from the indicator phrase supply the letters

explanation.surface: Pointed pegs or something similar are needed for a child's knitted pullover.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper suggests a British sweater, but it is a small creature that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is famous for leaping long distances on its powerful back legs.

clue.text: Where one may take a look back, on reflection?

definitions.text: Where one may take a look back, on reflection?

parts.words: Where one may take a look back, on reflection?
parts.note: surface reading: a place to sit and think over past events
setter's reading: a driver glances behind by means of a mirror image

explanation.walkthrough: On reflection usually means after more thought; here it is literal, a reflected view of the road behind a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's interior glass lets a driver see traffic behind without turning round.

clue.text: Joint wretched, get to work

parts.note: a knuckle is a finger joint
feeling down is feeling miserable

explanation.surface: Someone with a painful joint is told to stop moaning and start working.
explanation.definitionFit: To knuckle down is an idiom for applying oneself seriously to a task.

clue.text: Sense organ is aware, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it says to go by how the words are spoken, not their spelling

parts.note: someone who is aware of something knows it

explanation.surface: A playful question about whether an organ of sense has awareness.
explanation.definitionFit: The facial feature used for smelling is one of the five bodily sensory organs.

clue.text: Serious criminal misused rifle

indicators.note: something misused is handled wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dangerous offender has been using a gun illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a life sentence has committed a grave offence such as murder.

clue.text: Weaponry secure when turned over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the word is read from its last letter

parts.note: snug means safe and secure

explanation.surface: Arms are safe once they have been handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Firearms collectively make up an arsenal of weapons.

clue.text: Unconscious fusion of French and German articles

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
der is a German definite article

explanation.surface: Sounds like a linguistics paper on blending French and German grammar words.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural articles is shared: one article from French, one from German.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who is under has been put to sleep by anaesthetic before surgery.

clue.text: Note refreshing substance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the keynote of a musical scale
second meaning: a reviving medicine or mixer drink

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it seems to be a memo about a drink; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In music it names the first degree of a scale; elsewhere it is a pick-me-up or quinine water.

clue.text: Feller missing last bit of mustard in a sandwich, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone badly wrong, so the remaining letters are scrambled
missing means lacking, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of mustard, to be removed

explanation.surface: A man is unhappy that his sandwich has no mustard in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Feller looks like 'fellow', but it means something that fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorised saw with a toothed loop is the standard tool for cutting down trees.

clue.text: Who had wrong seat on jumbo?

indicators.note: wrong means incorrect, so the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks which airline passenger took the wrong seat on a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo suggests a jet, but it is an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A howdah is a canopied carriage fixed on an elephant's back for riders.

clue.text: Revolution supporting Irish county in economic decline

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: County Down is in Northern Ireland
a turn is one revolution

explanation.surface: Political upheaval backing an Irish county during a recession.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a slump in business activity or the wider market.

clue.text: Fat sovereign in store

parts.note: lard is pig fat
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An overweight monarch is spotted in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also an old British gold coin, but here it is the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool cupboard or pantry where household food is kept.

clue.text: Hone language at university

parts.note: Polish is the language of Poland
in British usage a student is up at university

explanation.surface: A student refines a foreign language while studying at college.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish up a skill is to refine and improve it, just as one sharpens a blade.

clue.text: Theme in story, yarn

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a running strand of a narrative
second meaning: spun fibre for sewing

explanation.walkthrough: Yarn seems to mean a tale, fitting the story, but it is the fibre sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a connecting line of plot and a fine strand of cotton for stitching.

clue.text: Dip bird in pond?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to plunge or lower the head quickly
second meaning: a waterfowl that swims

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to dunk a bird; the verb and the creature are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for bobbing down sharply and the name of a common waterfowl.

clue.text: Country that's fragile

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large nation in East Asia

definitions.note: a phrase meaning something that is breakable, standing for a noun

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a comment on a nation's instability; the second part names breakable porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the Asian nation is also the word for fine porcelain crockery, which breaks easily.

clue.text: Spots: one mopping up unknown number

indicators.note: mopping something up means soaking it in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
n is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A teenager counts pimples while one cream absorbs an untold number of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is the skin condition that brings out pimples, especially in adolescence.

clue.text: Part of church where wasps seen, odd ones swatted?

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are knocked out, leaving only the evens

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these words

explanation.surface: Pictures wasps in a church corner, with a few being swatted.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded or vaulted recess at the eastern end of a church building.

clue.text: Fashionable, some kitsch, I confess

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so part of the following words is taken

parts.note: letters running across the end of kitsch, I, and the start of confess

explanation.surface: Someone admits that a little kitsch is stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic describes something stylish and elegant, in vogue.

clue.text: Yes! Trick entertains us, good day for object of schoolboy humour

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so pieces sit inside

parts.note: whoopee is a cry of delight
a con is a swindle
taken as written
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A joyful shout as a prank amuses everyone on a good day for a childish joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good day' is a greeting, so it stands for the short word people say on meeting, not a date.
explanation.definitionFit: This inflatable rubber prank makes a rude noise when sat on, a classic juvenile gag.

clue.text: One's cut after two are joined

definitions.text: One's cut after two are joined

parts.words: One's cut after two are joined
parts.note: surface reading: something is severed after a pair of pieces is fastened together
setter's reading: a couple marry, and then a celebratory dessert is sliced

explanation.walkthrough: Joined suggests carpentry or splicing; it means joined in matrimony.
explanation.definitionFit: Newlyweds traditionally slice the tiered confection together at the reception after the ceremony.
